Late legendary graphic designer Susan Kare recently delivered a speech at the Startup School 2026 event, and her talk video has already been uploaded to Y Combinator's YouTube channel. You can watch it below.

Susan Kare shared wonderful stories and design insights

Over 40 years after the launch of the first-generation Macintosh, the system's graphics, fonts, icons, and overall UI elements still look as outstanding as they did back then.

In fact, many of the original elements Susan Kare designed for the first-generation Macintosh, whether in spirit or in practice, can still be seen in today's macOS. From the Command key symbol, the smiling Mac icon at startup, the system font, to the hand cursor, Kare's work not only shaped the visual language of the Mac, but also influenced the entire personal computer industry.

Although anyone who has studied Apple's history may have seen Kare's sketches, and even read or heard her interviews recounting the experience of that early work, hearing her personally recount the passion and frustrations of those years is always so fascinating—after all, in those days, graphical user interfaces and pixel graphics were still uncharted territory.

Therefore, if you're interested in design, Apple's history, or simply want to hear someone who has devoted a lifetime to a field they love discuss their profession from an expert perspective, Kare's talk is absolutely not to be missed.

In addition to detailing her work at Apple in detail, Kare also talked about how she joined the company, showed works created after she left, shared some little stories from Apple's early days, and quoted memorable lines from other legendary designers to bring the audience additional inspiration.
